newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA SHARE INDEX SHEDS 2.61 PCT.
newsitem.headline: MANILA SHARE INDEX SHEDS 2.61 PCT.

text.p: The Philippine stock market's main index buckled further at midtrade on Monday on selling in most blue chips, traders said.
The main index lost 69.13 points, or 2.61 percent, to 2,578.69.
Turnover was meagre at only over 400 million pesos in midsession.
Anscor-Hagedorn Securities vice-president Noel Reyes said profit-taking weighed down blue chip issues such as Meralco B, Ayala Land Inc and Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co.
"There's foreign selling, the big boys are getting out but there's no volume. They are unconvinced that the recent eight-day run-up was sustainable," said Reyes.
All indices were lower at midsession with the property sub-index leading the fall by 3.93 percent at 1,280.54 points.

"The selling started last Thursday, turned heavier on Friday and with the Dow significantly lower, we are just feeling the pressure as well," said Juanis Barredo, technical analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
The Dow Jones fell 156.78 points settling at 8,031.22 last Friday.
